children.translated_text: Seated on the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, the God of gods, the lord of the world,
the goddess <s>Pārvatī</s> asked about a truth exceedingly hard to obtain.
<s>Pārvatī</s> said:
O god, graciously tell me the marks of gemstones,
by which purified practitioners attain accomplishment here.
O <s>Mahādeva</s>, O very terrible one, they bring about the crushing of enemies,
and here they produce poetic power and long life, O lord.

children.text: aṣṭau guṇāḥ phalaṃ yatra tvatprasādān maheśvara
children.translated_text: Where, by your grace, O <s>Maheśvara</s>, there is the fruit of eight qualities,

children.text: jñānamārgaṃ ca mokṣam ca śūlarogaṃ ca dāruṇam ||
children.translated_text: the path of knowledge and liberation, and relief from the severe disease of colic,
from eye disease, head disease, and the affliction of poison as well,

children.text: sphuṭaṃ vada yathā prabho prasādān me maheśvara ||
children.translated_text: tell me clearly how this is so, O lord, through your favor, O <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: uvāca śaṃkaro devi yat tvayā paripṛcchyate
children.translated_text: <s>Śaṃkara</s> said: O goddess, what you have asked,

children.text: yan na kasyacid ākhyātaṃ tad vadāmi varānane ||
children.translated_text: which has not been told to anyone, that I shall tell you, fair-faced one.

children.text: purāhaṃ viṣṇunā yukto brahmaṇā saha sundari
children.translated_text: Formerly, O beautiful one, I went together with <s>Viṣṇu</s> and with <s>Brahmā</s>,
to <s>Śuklatīrtha</s>, O goddess, on the splendid bank of the <s>Revā</s>.
There stands a mountain named <s>Ratnaparvata</s>,
established by <s>Indra</s>, O goddess, and bringing happiness to all the gods.
By merely seeing it one is released from all sins;
a sick person becomes free from disease; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: devyā āyatane ye tu citāṃ dahanti mānavāḥ
children.translated_text: Those people who burn a funeral pyre in the temple of the goddess
go to the supreme place, joined with the sight of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: aṣṭamyāṃ snāti yaḥ kuṇḍe pūjayitvā tataḥ śivam
children.translated_text: Whoever bathes in the pool on the eighth lunar day, after first worshipping <s>Śiva</s>,
is freed from all sins and comes to my world.

children.text: itthaṃ devagaṇāḥ sarve kuṇḍe snātvā kṣaṇaṃ sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: In this way all the hosts of gods bathed in the pool and remained there for a moment;
with bodies purified and prosperous, they then returned to <s>Kedāra</s>.
The liṅga established by <s>Garutmat</s> removes all sins;
the mere sight of it drives away the sin of killing a Brahmin.
On the eighth and fourteenth lunar days, and especially on the full-moon day,

children.text: yaḥ pūjayati puṇyātmā mama lokaṃ sa gacchati ||
children.translated_text: the meritorious person who worships it goes to my world.

children.text: kedāraṃ pūjayed yas tu puṇyātmā bhāgyabhājanam
children.translated_text: The meritorious person who worships <s>Kedāra</s>, the object of fortunate destiny,
obtains the supreme state, endowed with the accomplishment of all aims.

children.text: indreṇa sthāpitaṃ vajraṃ kośaś ca dhanadena tu
children.translated_text: The thunderbolt was established by <s>Indra</s>, and the treasure by the giver of wealth;

children.text: mayāpi sthāpitā mantrāḥ kathitaṃ te varānane ||
children.translated_text: I too established the mantras. This has been told to you, fair-faced one.
From the eruptions of <s>Garutmat</s> there issued the great river <s>Maṇikalā</s>,
of great splendor and destructive of all sins.
Through her power, O goddess, the gemstones have auspicious marks;
they bestow enjoyment and liberation, and they ward off the faults that cause disease.
The blessed goddess said:
Tell me the marks of gemstones as they truly are, O bull-bannered one.

children.text: kenopāyena te grāhyā devapūjā kathaṃ vibho ||
children.translated_text: By what method should they be taken, and how is divine worship to be performed, O lord?

children.text: kīdṛśaṃ ca vrataṃ kāryaṃ kiṃ dānaṃ kasya pūjanam
children.translated_text: What kind of vow should be undertaken, what gift should be given, and whom should one worship?

children.text: kā ca bhaktikriyā kāryā deva me vada bhairava ||
children.translated_text: And what act of devotion should be performed? Tell me, O god, O <s>Bhairava</s>.
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> said:
Having gone to the abode of <s>Kedāra</s>, with eight hundred pitchers,
for glorious <s>Kedāranātha</s>, forming the intention in his mind,
and having worshipped the guardian of the field according to his ability with unsurpassed offerings,
the practitioner, desiring the fruit, should do so with care.

children.text: evaṃ pūjya mahābhaktyā praṇamya ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus worshipped with great devotion and bowed again and again,

children.text: baliṃ dadyād vidhānena dikṣu sarvāsu yatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should carefully offer bali (ritual oblation) according to rule in all the directions.
Japa (mantra recitation) is to be performed at the place of <s>Śiva</s>, honored by the gods;
then, going to the great river, he sees the jewel-stones.
With his body bound by mantras and adorned with a coating of gojihvā,

children.text: atha teṣāṃ maṇīnāṃ tu kartavyaṃ suparīkṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: then he must make a careful examination of those gemstones.

children.text: gopitaṃ yan mayā pūrvaṃ tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
children.translated_text: Hear from me as I tell what was formerly hidden by me:
it has the appearance of well-heated gold and is furnished with blue lines;
it always bears a white line and is joined with a yellow line;
it is connected with a reddish line and adorned with a black line.

children.text: etaiś cihnaiḥ samāyukto nīlakaṇṭha iti smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: A stone furnished with these marks is remembered as <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>;
it grants abundant enjoyments and the very hard-to-obtain path of knowledge.
It produces poetic power and long life; there is no doubt about this.
One that has a star-like appearance, a golden color, and is adorned with four spots,
and that bears a black spot and has a luster like a cat's eye,
will bring gain of wealth; no deliberation is needed about this.
One with the color of a red tree, with a brilliance like sapphire,
and joined with a white line, is of great splendor for matters of wealth.
It is known as <s>Viṣṇu</s> and bestows the fruit of every lordly prosperity.
One resembling pure crystal and adorned with a blue line,
white and bearing a black spot, is a gem that grants all desires.

children.text: pītaś ca śvetarekhaś ca maṇiḥ svacchaś ca dṛśyate
children.translated_text: A yellow gem, with a white line and clear in appearance, is seen;

children.text: guṇānām ākaraḥ so hi bahurogān nihanti ca ||
children.translated_text: it is indeed a mine of virtues and destroys many diseases.
One that resembles a pigeon's throat and is marked with white spots,
born in the lineage of <s>Āstīka</s>, is a gem that removes the pride of poison.
A radiant gem like the eye of a sāraṅga deer, shaped like the eye of a rutting elephant,

children.text: śvetair bindubhir anvito varatanur bhāsvān maṇir bindukaḥ
children.translated_text: endowed with white spots, beautiful in body and shining, is the gem called <s>Binduka</s>.
By the procedure of drinking water with which it has been washed, severe poison is destroyed.

children.text: yat sarvaṃ vinatāsuto bahuvidhaṃ hanyād viṣaṃ dāruṇam
children.translated_text: Whatever manifold terrible poison the son of <s>Vinatā</s> would destroy,

children.text: saṃgrāme jayate ripūn bahuvidhān bhogān maṇir yacchati ||
children.translated_text: that gem conquers many kinds of enemies in battle and grants enjoyments.
Somewhat blue-footed, then reddish in hue, and somewhat lightning-like in brilliance,
Somewhat bright to the eye, furnished with many kinds of lines, and round,

children.text: vikhyātaḥ sa mahāmaṇir viṣaharo baddho narāṇāṃ kare
children.translated_text: that great jewel is famous as a remover of poison when bound on men's hands.

children.text: bhūtaṃ nāśayatīha somasadṛśas tasmāt pṛthivyāṃ priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here it destroys spirits; resembling the moon, it is therefore beloved on earth.
Having the equal radiance of many jewels, marked with clusters of many kinds of lines,
pure, furnished with groups of dots, spotless, and removing the pride of the lord of serpents,
truly that jewel was created by me to bring the acquisition of gold and wealth.

children.text: prakhyātaś ca sa siddhajanmajananaiḥ puṇyaiḥ satāṃ gocaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: And it is renowned, accessible to the good through the meritorious births that produce accomplished beings.
But the one that is blue in color and adorned with five dots,
pure-limbed, reddish, and round, is famous as <s>Vinatāsuta</s>.
If on its body there is a shining line like the color of vermilion,
it should be known as dark-colored and as crushing all poison without remainder.
The one that is bronze-colored and filled with many lines,
scattered with many dots, removes fever and burning heat.

children.text: pītavarṇo bhaved yas tu dvirekhaḥ sitabindukaḥ
children.translated_text: The one that is yellow in color, with two lines and white dots,
destroys even the very terrible poison of an old scorpion.
A white and yellow, even line, with the equal radiance of sapphire,

children.text: netrarogaṃ ca śūlaṃ ca jalapānād vyapohati ||
children.translated_text: removes eye disease and pain through the drinking of water.
The one that is green in color and adorned with a white line,
joined with a yellow line, removes poison completely.
The one that is yellow like wheat, again with the shape of an elephant's eye,
always bearing white dots, destroys possession by spirits and indigestion.

children.text: raktāṅgaḥ śuddharekhaś ca ardhāṅge kṛṣṇa eva ca
children.translated_text: Red-bodied and with a pure line, and black on half of its body,

children.text: sa maṇī raktaśūlaṃ ca netraśūlaṃ vyapohati ||
children.translated_text: that jewel removes blood-pain and eye-pain.
Resembling pure crystal, somewhat red and yellow,

children.text: vṛścikānāṃ viṣaṃ hanti sa maṇiḥ sarvakāmadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that jewel destroys the poison of scorpions and grants every desire.

children.text: ratkam ardhaṃ ca kṛṣṇārdhaṃ śvetaṃ kiṃcid bhaved yadi
children.translated_text: If one half is red, one half black, and a little white,
the one that has such a form destroys the poison of snakes and the like.

children.text: raktāṅgo raktarekhaś ca āvartaiḥ śobhanair yutaḥ
children.translated_text: Red-bodied, with red lines, and furnished with beautiful whorls,
that jewel should be known as <s>Garuḍa</s>, destroyer of the poison of snakes and the like.
Yellow-bodied, with black lines, and filled with many dots,
the one that has such a form removes the poison of great serpents.
Yellow-bodied, with yellow lines, and adorned with a red line,
white and remover of all diseases, it has been described, O lovely-faced one.
Resembling a flower of <s>kūṣmāṇḍī</s>, and of many forms through its dots,
it should be known as remover of all diseases and crusher of every poison.
Those that here are red in color, filled with many dots,
brilliant and exceedingly beautiful, all of them are crushers of poison.
With a dot as its navel, of great brilliance, adorned with a black dot,
this has been described to you, O lovely-faced one, as destroyer of all disease.
Shining with the yellow color of madder and furnished with coppery dots,
it is always remover of all diseases and destroyer of fever caused by spirits.
Resembling a pomegranate flower and adorned with a black dot,
splendid, producing good fortune, and furnished with a bee-like line, O beloved.
Resembling a jasmine flower, round in equal measure, O beloved,
endowed with such a form, it crushes every poison.
The one whose shape is like an elephant's eye and whose splendor equals a cat's eye,
with great brilliance equal to <s>Tārkṣya</s>, is worthy of worship when duly honored.
It is seen as making a sacred ford, very brilliant, and radiant.

children.text: samastaviṣaho jñeyaḥ sa maṇir jīyate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: That jewel should certainly be known as enduring and as bearing all poisons.
